notes:
# A meeting being recorded says so on its own page {video}
Open a meeting that has recorded before while it is recording again and the
page said "Recorded successfully" over the file from last time. The badge now
says what is happening -- Recording now, or the step the run is on, or
Reading the recording while the analysis runs -- and a card above the files
says when this run started and that its file appears when it ends.

# Two runs of one meeting can be made into one file {film}
Merging only ever knew about the parts of a single capture. A run that ends
outright -- the Mac slept, the app was replaced, somebody pressed Stop -- is
followed by a NEW run with a name of its own, so one meeting sat in two cards
with nothing offering to join them. The first card now says "2 recordings"
and offers to merge them all, oldest first, whenever they were made. It names
what it will join before it runs, because two runs of a repeating meeting can
just as easily be two different days.

# And the parts can go, once the merge is checked {trash}
Merging left two copies of the same meeting on disk, which on a long meeting
is gigabytes. The app now offers to move the originals to the Trash -- but
only after measuring the file that came out: ffmpeg can abandon a join
halfway and still leave something playable, so a merged file that plays for
less than its parts did deletes nothing and says why.

# Every mark in What's new has a picture {sparkle}
The headings in these notes carry a glyph name typed by hand, and a name SF
Symbols has never heard of draws nothing at all — so the What's new list had
blank tiles in it. The names now go through the app's own table, and one it
cannot place falls back to a glyph rather than to a hole.

# New meeting no longer resizes the window {plus}
Pressing ⌘N on a normal window used to make the window jump wider: the form
was built side by side before anything had measured it, and macOS answers a
layout that needs more room by growing the window. The form now asks the pane
how much room there is, so New leaves the window exactly as it was — and a
wide window still opens the two cards side by side.

# Invitations read the way the mail reads {envelope}
A webinar called “Joey Yap’s Unlock The Palace” arrived from an HTML mail
body as “Joey Yap's Unlock The Palace”, and that is what the list showed.
Names and senders are now unescaped wherever they are drawn, searched or
imported — including the rows already sitting in the cache.

# A licence key can arrive as a link {link}
A receipt or the website can now open `recordlah://activate?key=…` and the
app fills the key in for you. It FILLS IT AND WAITS: any web page can open a
custom scheme, so one that activated by itself would be a page on the
internet deciding which licence this Mac holds — and on a multi-seat licence,
spending a seat nobody offered. The typing was the hard part; the press is
yours. A link carrying anything else does nothing at all.

# A run that has stopped stops saying it is running {clock}
The Logs window read the ending out of the log and knew four of them; a run
that stopped any other way — before the meeting started, or because the link
never opened Zoom — was still showing “In progress” half an hour later. It
knows those endings now, and where it cannot name one it looks at when the
log was last written instead: nothing has written to it for ninety seconds
means the run has gone, whatever it said on the way out.

# A link that goes nowhere says so instead of sitting there {link}
A link the browser opens is given fifteen minutes to become a Zoom link,
because a lobby can count down for that long and an invite can redirect when
the meeting opens. A mistyped link is not on its way anywhere, so the row sat
on “Opening the event page” for a quarter of an hour with nothing happening.
A page that has not moved in two and a half minutes, is not Zoom's and has no
prompt to answer now ends the run with “Link went nowhere”.

# The microphone settings, in two lines {mic}
A name and its control on each line -- the input with the way to try it, then
what it is hearing and whether macOS is allowing it -- instead of four things
across with hairlines between them. It reads as a short form rather than a
strip of instruments, and it is what lets this page fit the window the
meetings list fits.

# Settings fits the window the meetings list fits {macwindow}
Opening Settings › Recording used to widen the window, because the page
asked for about 1,300 points — more than this window's own minimum. Three
things were asking: a note whose two sentences each wanted a full line, the
capture cards' descriptions, and the microphone row's four parts side by
side. The note and the cards now wrap or truncate into the room they are
given, and the microphone row goes one part above another under about 960
points, hairlines and all. Measured at every width from 1043 to 1600:
opening Settings leaves the window exactly where it was.

# Coming back from Settings shows the meetings again {macwindow}
The pane that is not showing is taken off the stage so it stops holding the
window open — but the meetings list was put there when the window was built,
and taking it off dropped the constraints that hold it in place, so going
back to it showed an empty page. It stays where it was put; only the two
pages built on demand come and go.

# Visiting Settings no longer holds the window open {macwindow}
The three tabs are built once and kept, and the ones you are not looking at
were merely hidden — a hidden view keeps its constraints, so one visit to
Settings › Recording left that page's own minimum width propping the window
open for the rest of the session. The meetings list could not be made narrow
again, and neither could the window. A pane that is not showing is off the
stage now; it keeps its state and stops being a floor under a page nobody is
looking at.

# Testing the microphone no longer resizes the window {sliders}
The button says three different things while a test runs — “Test
microphone”, “Recording… say something”, “Playing back…” — and it was sized
to each in turn, so the row grew and shrank and took the window with it. It
is now as wide as the longest thing it will say, decided once.

# The microphone row reads in light mode too {sun}
The level meter's unlit bars were the system's label colour at a tenth, which
on a white card is very nearly white — so in light mode there was no meter
until something lit it. They use the palette's own track grey now. The meter
is also as tall as the input beside it, so the two captions sit on one line
rather than "Input level" riding above "Input", and Refresh is a glyph beside
the Input caption instead of a button in the card's heading, where it was cut
off by the edge of the card.

# Saving settings no longer races itself {shield}
Reading this Mac's displays imported part of Quartz on first use, and that
import is not thread-safe: asked for from two threads at once — saving the
settings page while the level meter runs — it could raise from inside PyObjC
and take the save with it. It is resolved once, when the module loads.

# The storage bar shows what is left {sliders}
The empty end of it was drawn in the same grey as the card behind it — three
points apart in the dark — so the bar looked like it simply stopped where the
grey did, with no way to see how much of the disk is still free. It has a
ground of its own now, in both appearances, and the swatch beside “free of”
matches it.

# A finished meeting's name is not what gives way {macwindow}
On a narrow window the four buttons beside it took the width and the name was
cut to "New…" — the one thing on the page that says which recording you are
looking at. The buttons drop to a line of their own now, and the name keeps
the width. A status pill is measured rather than left to hug, too: it was
stretching into a coloured bar across the line whenever there was slack.

# The microphone row looks like the rest of the app {gear}
The input is chosen from the app's own dropdown now — the shape the Folder
and Time zone fields use — rather than a stock macOS pop-up that was 24
points tall with its own bezel and its own font. A hairline sits between each
of the four: the input, the level, the test and the access.

# A restarted capture keeps your voice {mic}
A capture that restarts — a Zoom window swap is enough — asked for the
microphone only on the first attempt, so a meeting could come back with part
one holding your half of the conversation and part two without it.

# A finished recording says whose voices are in it {mic}
Your voice — Included, or The meeting only — sits with Duration, File size
and Recorded on the recording card. Recorded against the FILE when it is
made, not worked out afterwards: the setting and the meeting's own choice can
both be changed later, and a recording would then claim to hold a voice it
was made without. Recordings made before this says nothing rather than guess.

# The buttons over a finished recording have room to breathe {sliders}
Edit details, Logs and Duplicate were stock macOS buttons, which are 21
points tall whatever is in them — so a glyph filled one corner to corner with
no air above or below. They are the app's own buttons now, the same ones on
the card underneath.

# And loud enough to make out {sliders}
The microphone was mixed at half, on the reasoning that a mic on the desk is
louder than a meeting coming back over the network. That is not true of the
one most people are wearing — a headset mic is quiet and band-limited before
it reaches us — so it goes in at full now, with the peaks held inside the
rails rather than the whole thing kept quiet. `zoomcap --mic-gain N` moves it
either way for a recording that needs it.

# And it plays back at the speed you said it {mic}
macOS hands the microphone over as ONE channel at 24 kHz — the rate a
Bluetooth headset works at — while the meeting arrives as TWO at 48 kHz.
Taken across sample for sample, a voice played four times too fast: twice for
the rate, and twice again for being read as a stereo pair. The microphone is
now brought to one channel at the meeting's own rate before anything is mixed,
and the same voice goes into both channels.

# Your own voice actually reaches the recording {mic}
The microphone was captured, converted and counted — and then thrown away.
The meeting's audio arrives as two separate channels, and the code that reads
it asked CoreMedia for room for one, so every attempt to mix the two came back
empty and the recording fell back to the meeting alone. Fixed, along with two
things it was hiding: the writer was being handed audio in two different
shapes, which makes it fail the whole file, and a failed writer now says so in
the log instead of leaving a 0-byte recording.

# Intel Macs and older macOS can still record {shield}
Microphone capture is a macOS 15 feature, and asking for it unconditionally
raised what the recorder needs to macOS 26 and dropped Intel Macs altogether.
It is asked for only where it exists now, and the recorder is a universal
binary again — on an older Mac the meeting records as it always did.

# The Recording card, in two halves {mic}
What a recording CONTAINS and what is made of it afterwards are two
questions, so they are two tiles now rather than two rows of switches: Your
microphone, with the three-way choice and what “Use default” comes out as
for this meeting, and AI notes, with the switch and a box to type the question in — typed where it is asked rather than behind a sheet. They
sit side by side on a wide window and one above the other on a narrow one,
breaking at the same width the two cards above them do — so the form is
either two columns or one, never a mix of both.

# The New meeting form no longer moves the window {sliders}
Opening it snapped the window to a size of its own, and picking an option
inside it moved the window again — the three-segment strip is a fixed width,
and tied to the edge of its tile it made the whole window exactly that wide,
which also meant the window could not be dragged afterwards. The strip hugs
its own labels now, the way the Repeats strip above it always has.

# The Meeting details mark is the size of the others {info}
The heading's glyph was SF Symbols' bare letter i — taller than it is wide,
so it grew until it filled its tile and read as one size larger than the
calendar and the mic beside it. It is the circled i now, and no tile glyph is
ever scaled up past the size it was asked for.

# The Recording card lines up {mic}
“Analyse when the meeting ends” sat twelve points further in than the label
under it, padded inside a box nothing draws. The row now starts where the
rest of the card starts, and its switch ends where the box under it ends.

# The analysis estimate is readable in full {clock}
“About 1 hour 3 minutes” was cut off at “About 1 hour 3 mi…” in the consent
screen. The three figures now wrap onto a second line instead of truncating,
and the three tiles stay the same height.

# A spent free trial says so where it matters {sparkle}
The offer to record a meeting you joined yourself read “0 trial recordings
left” beside a blue Start recording button. It now says “No recordings left”
in a colour that means it, with View plans beside it — and the offer stays up
while the plans are read, because the meeting is still running.

---

Everything else in this release:

- Merging is offered across a meeting's separate runs, not only within one.
- A run that is stopped outright no longer leaves the read view describing
  the run before it.
- `install.sh` refuses to replace the app while a recording is running, and
  quits only the window -- the recorder and the window are the same binary,
  and "quit RecordLah before installing" once cost a meeting nine minutes in.
- The flag beside a time zone lines up with the words it belongs to:
  on the place name in the picker's list, and on the value in the
  field on the form.
